title: Sizing before reading
purpose: Tells an agent how much a file or folder will cost to read. For a file it gives bytes, lines, an estimated token count, and an outline: functions, classes and methods with their line ranges for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, C#, Java and Go, headings for Markdown, and top-level keys for JSON and YAML, so the agent reads only the lines it needs. For a folder it gives a tree of totals, largest first, and names the largest files.
inputs: A file or folder in the workspace, stdin, or `--text`, with `--language` for stdin and text. For a folder, `--depth` sets how deep the tree goes and `--top` how many of the largest files to name.
verifies: Each symbol's first line is read again to confirm it names the symbol, ranges and nesting are checked, JSON and YAML keys are held against the parser's, and folder totals are added up two ways.
limits: Token counts are an estimate, a quarter of the characters, not any model's tokenizer, and the output says so. Code outlines come from a quick scan of the source, not a compiler. A file it can't outline (binary, an unsupported type, a parse error, over 8 MiB) is still counted, with the reason.
